LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. The defending World Champion Seattle Seahawks are coming to Mile High for a Thursday Night Football throwdown. It's a short-week turnaround for both teams, with the Broncos coming off a win and the Seahawks off a loss. Broncos-Seahawks was the Super Bowl many people expected last season before Bo Nix's shocking ankle injury. When the 2026 schedule dropped earlier this year, this game was circled as a potential Super Bowl preview. Despite both teams sitting at 3-2, few people currently view the Broncos as a true Super Bowl contender, but that's no different than the general consensus at this time last year. The narrative around the Seahawks, though, is strikingly different. What's the disconnect? Offense. The Broncos' offense and the quality of quarterback play haven't been at a Super Bowl level — but the season is still young. How will Broncos-Seahawks shake out on Thursday night? We're going around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff foresee this one playing out at Mile High. You can connect with each staff on X (their handles are linked next to their names). Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-1 : Another week where the Broncos decided to take the first three quarters off before finally showing up. At some point, it gets a little anticlimactic. That point, for me, is now. It worked against a winless, decimated Chargers team — even though Denver barely eked out a win — but it absolutely will not work against the reigning Super Bowl champs, who come into this game a little ticked off following a loss to San Francisco. Denver being home should help, but the magic won't be enough this time around. Fortunately, a much-needed mini-bye awaits. Payton might become the clubhouse leader for Coach of the Year if he can get this offense going. away.headline: Week 6 Injury Report: Seahawks at Broncos
away.blurb: Among those practicing fully on Wednesday was receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was listed as limited the previous two days because of an ankle injury. Smith-Njigba, who leads the NFL in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, does not have a game status on the final injury report, meaning he is good to go. Also without a status, despite being listed as limited all week with an ankle injury, is defensive lineman Leonard Williams, who played last week through the injury he suffered in a Week 4 win over the Chargers. Also ruled out are linebacker Chazz Surratt, who will miss a third straight game with a calf injury, and running back Zach Charbonnet, who remains on the physically unable to perform list as he works his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. For the Broncos, All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II has been ruled out with an ankle injury, as has starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). The Texans plan to play Harrison this week, and the Jaguars and head coach Liam Coen have already said that preparing for Harrison and his skill-set is already underway. With that said, I just do not see him doing much against the Jaguars. The Jaguars give up a decent amount of yards and catches to outside receivers as a function of their scheme, but Harrison is the same receiver who has struggled to get open all year. I like both Jarrian Jones and Travis Hunter in coverage against Harrison this week, which I think will lead to a small day of production for the Texans' new receiver. It was Brenton Strange two weeks ago and Parker Washington last week, but I believe it is going to go in Meyers' direction this week for a few reasons. For one, the Texans have been one of the best defenses in the NFL against tight ends this season. They also do have a potential hole in the slot, which could mean a big day for Washington, but I think they are going to try to roll coverage to him and give him extra attention. I think this is a week where the matchup is going to favor Jakobi Meyers. It was Brenton Strange two weeks ago and Parker Washington last week, but I believe it is going to go in Meyers' direction this week for a few reasons. For one, the Texans have been one of the best defenses in the NFL against tight ends this season. They also do have a potential hole in the slot, which could mean a big day for Washington, but I think they are going to try to roll coverage to him and give him extra attention. That brings us to Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers on the outside, where the Texans have struggled. The Texans' pair of outside cornerbacks have allowed 16 combined explosive receptions through five games, while the Texans are the worst team in the entire NFL at defending wide receiver targets based on EPA/Play -- even worse than the Tennessee Titans, Detroit Lions, and Miami Dolphins. With that said, I think Meyers is the one who will benefit more so against that matchup this week. According to NextGenStats, Thomas has been targeted on 2 of his 17 deep routes this season (11.8%), after being targeted on 27 of his 87 deep routes in 2024 (31.0%). Thomas has been targeted on six deep passes with Stingley in coverage in his career and has not caught any of them with Stingley intercepting one. This likely means Meyers draws the better matchups, and he has the kind of tough skill-set that translates to this kind of matchup. I expect a lot of Meyers this week. But the numbers beneath those records leave room for a considerably less predictable afternoon in London. Jacksonville enters as a 2.5-point favorite after escaping Philadelphia 19-17. Houston finally broke through by beating Tennessee 26-3, then acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. These predictions deliberately push beyond a narrow upset or another respectable quarterback performance. The forecast: Houston produces its most complete game of the season. CJ Stroud throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Jacksonville's defense allows only 14 points per game, second in the NFL. Predicting four passing touchdowns against that unit is aggressive, but its strength against the run can obscure a vulnerable pass defense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Jaguars surrender 277.2 passing yards per game, ranking 30th. Conversely, they allow an NFL-best 63.8 rushing yards per game and just 2.9 yards per carry. Houston therefore has good reason to attack through Stroud rather than repeatedly challenge Jacksonville's strongest area. Stroud has already thrown for 1,402 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions through five games. Against Tennessee, he completed 26 of 34 attempts for 261 yards, including an impressive eight completions on 11 pressured throws for 115 yards. The prediction requires Houston to convert passing volume into touchdowns, something it has not consistently accomplished. Harrison's arrival creates another possible weapon, although his debut and workload remain uncertain. This call rests primarily on Stroud's existing production and Jacksonville's passing-yardage vulnerability, not an assumption that the newcomer immediately dominates. Will Anderson Jr. records four sacks as Houston forces three turnovers Anderson delivered three of Houston's four sacks against Tennessee, providing the foundation for an even bigger prediction against Jacksonville. Four sacks by one player would be a spectacular follow-up, not merely continued improvement. The Texans limited the Titans to 187 total yards and three points after DeMeco Ryans reclaimed defensive play-calling duties. Tennessee's struggling offense makes that result an imperfect measuring stick, but Houston still ranks ninth in yards allowed per play. Jacksonville presents a tougher opponent, yet Sunday exposed pressure points. Trevor Lawrence threw an interception and lost a fumble against Philadelphia despite producing 331 passing yards and two touchdowns. Houston must turn disruptive plays into possession changes, rather than simply allowing Jacksonville to reset after sacks. The Jaguars' penalty problems could help create those opportunities. They have committed at least 13 penalties and accumulated more than 100 penalty yards in consecutive games. Backward movement makes passing situations more predictable, giving Anderson additional chances to attack. The bold call is four Anderson sacks and three Houston takeaways: pressure converts Jacksonville's mistakes into decisive field-position advantages. The Texans win by at least 17 points Jacksonville's winning record and scoring defense make a comfortable Houston victory the biggest leap here. The Jaguars have allowed only 70 points across five games, while the Texans entered last Sunday without a win. Nevertheless, a blowout becomes plausible if the first two predictions connect. Houston's passing offense attacks Jacksonville's statistical weakness, while turnovers supply short fields and prevent Lawrence from answering every score. Jacksonville also needed a 53-yard kickoff return and Cam Little's 57-yard field goal to escape Philadelphia. That extraordinary finish demonstrated resilience, but it should not conceal how close the Jaguars came to losing. Stroud's four touchdown passes power the offense, and defensive disruption keeps the Jaguars from turning their rushing balance into sustained control. London delivers a division-changing upset, not another last-second escape. Jacksonville enters the game at 4-1 after a dramatic 17-16 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, sealed by Cam Little's 57 yard field goal in the final seconds. Houston is 1-4 but comes into the matchup with renewed confidence after earning its first win of the season, a convincing 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Kickoff is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET at Wembley Stadium, with coverage on NFL Network. C.J. Stroud Leads Houston's Offense Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud will be a key player to watch as Houston looks to continue its turnaround. Stroud threw for 261 yards and a touchdown against Tennessee, spreading the ball around to seven different receivers. His ability to distribute the football and make plays downfield will be important against a Jacksonville defense that has helped the Jaguars get off to a strong start. Houston also recently added wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. Harrison reunites with Stroud after their time together at Ohio State, giving the Texans another potential weapon in the passing game. Head coach DeMeco Ryans will also want his defense to maintain the intensity it showed against Tennessee. Houston limited the Titans to just three points and 187 total yards, providing an encouraging sign after a difficult opening month. Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars Look to Continue Winning Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence leads a Jaguars offense that has helped the team build a 4-1 record. Head coach Liam Coen has Jacksonville playing competitive football, and the team's ability to find ways to win close games has been important during its early-season success. The Jaguars will look to establish their offense and take advantage of opportunities against Houston. However, Jacksonville must also adjust along the offensive line after left tackle Anton Harrison suffered a knee injury against Philadelphia. Walker Little is expected to step into the starting role, creating an important challenge against Houston's pass rush. An Important AFC South Battle Sunday's matchup gives Houston an opportunity to build on its first victory and make progress within the division. Jacksonville, meanwhile, can continue its strong start and maintain its position near the top of the AFC South. With Stroud looking to keep Houston's offense moving and Lawrence leading a Jacksonville team that has found ways to win, the London matchup offers an important test for both sides.

A preseason favorite of many to contend for the Super Bowl, Houston finally got into the win column last week with an impressive 26-3 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville. For the first time this season, the highly touted Texans dominated defensively, limiting Tennessee to just three points and 187 Total Yards. C.J. Stroud connected on passes to seven different receivers and threw for 261 yards to lead the attack on offense. Jacksonville, meanwhile, won a game they may not have deserved but were glad to have been gifted. They knocked off the Eagles, 19-17, at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Philadelphia took the lead with eight seconds remaining. Jacksonville was without a timeout, but Ameer Abdullah managed to return the ensuing kickoff 53 yards in seven seconds. Cam Little then converted a 57-yard field goal as time expired to win the game for the Jags. Jacksonville has now won three straight. They lead the AFC South by two games over the Colts and three games over the Texans. Stroud and the Texans have moved the ball through the air (No. 4 in the NFL with 1402 yards), but only Green Bay has gained fewer yards on the ground (No. 31 with 395 yards). home.headline: Jaguars turn to Jacob Bobenmoyer after Ross Matiscik injury: Report
home.blurb: NFL MLB NBA NHL NCAA Football NCAA Basketball UFC/MMA PGA Tour Games JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS Jaguars sign Jacob Bobenmoyer to practice squad after Matiscik injury Jacob Bobenmoyer will take over snapping duties after DaVon Hamilton's emergency stint, per report. This story was updated to add new information. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. home.headline: Texans Injury Report: 4 Players Miss Practice Before Jaguars London Trip
home.blurb: And in all, four players wound up not participating, while a few others found their way onto the injury report as either a limited or full participant. Jul 31, 2026; Houston, TX, USA; Houston Texans running back British Brooks (44) and running back David Montgomery (32) and running back Woody Marks (4) during training camp at Houston Methodist Training Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect David Montgomery, Jalen Pitre Out as Expected David Montgomery, Jalen Pitre Out as Expected Two of the non-participants from the Texans' Wednesday practice were to be expected: that's running back David Montgomery, who's dealing with a groin injury, as well as defensive back Jalen Pitre, who suffered an AC joint sprain during last weekend's game against the Tennessee Titans. As of now, their status is considered week-to-week, meaning there's a good chance that both could be sidelined for Week 6 against the Jaguars, yet might not have to be forced on injured reserve, which would take them out for a minimum of four weeks. The two other DNPs from the Texans' practice— linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair and Trent Brown— have both been dealing with some nagging injuries through the past couple of weeks that effectively left them to sit out of Wednesday's practice. However, considering both played in last week's game against the Titans while dealing with their respective injuries, it'd be fair to assume that both are still on track to play in Week 6 against the Jaguars. Henry To'oTo'o Trending Up for Return The Texans officially activated the 21-day return window for Henry To'oTo'o on Wednesday, who's been sidelined for the past four weeks due to a shoulder injury he suffered in Week 1 against the Buffalo Bills. Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has missed each of the team's last three games since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season. Williams pumped his fist through tears as he was carted off the field in Chicago, leading many to believe he'd suffered a long-term injury. However, when reports later indicated that he suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain, many fans and analysts piled on with criticism of his dramatic reaction. Williams fired back at these critics when speaking with reporters on Thursday. Williams also said he was frustrated about how his injury was reported, saying all of the reports were incorrect. However, he would not go into any further detail regarding the true nature of his injury. Williams appears to be on track to play in Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons after notching full practice participation on Wednesday.

away.headline: Bears QB Caleb Williams addresses backlash he faced after injury
away.blurb: "I care about the team, the organization, winning, being out there, my teammates, all of that," Williams said Thursday. "I care, and that's the biggest thing. This is what I love to do. This puts a smile on my face. It's everything to me. So, not being able to be out there was frustrating. It was more the tears or whatever that was." Williams is trending toward a return to the field this Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. He's been a full participant in practice for two days (including Wednesday's walkthrough) and meeting with the media is also a strong indication. While Williams still has a stress test to pass and setbacks to avoid, if all goes well, the Bears will get back their star QB as they look to get back in the win column. Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams met with the media for the first time since suffering a torn hamstring in a Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , and he didn't hold back when addressing everything from the true nature of his injury to the backlash that he received for his emotional reaction. When Williams suffered his hamstring injury, he looked to be in intense pain, where he was helped off the field by trainers and later carted to the locker room as he waved to the Bears faithful cheering him on at Soldier Field. The reaction, to say the least, was ridiculous. While most people could understand the reason behind his reaction -- especially with the full extent unknown at the time -- there were plenty of people who ridiculed Williams and questioned his toughness. It didn't help that there were initial reports indicating that he wouldn't miss much time, when he in fact went on to miss nearly a month. Williams doesn't owe anyone an explanation for his emotions, but he explained them regardless while addressing the backlash he faced for getting emotional. home.headline: Michael Penix Jr. Injured, Falcons QB Updates Status & Return Timeline After Tua's Game-Ending INT
home.blurb: Injuries have been a massive story in Penix's career. The young quarterback only appeared in nine games last season after suffering a left ACL injury that required season-ending surgery. He missed the first two games of the NFL season but provided a spark upon his return, as Atlanta had won two games in a row heading into Sunday night. Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss against the Baltimore Ravens after taking a big hit in the pocket. On Thursday, however, he expressed optimism that he will be able to play in Week 6: After missing the Falcons' drive in overtime, Penix told reporters following the game that he doesn't believe it will be a long-term injury, per ESPN's Marc Raimondi : Head coach Kevin Stefanski had previously provided more information on the injured quarterback after the contest. "I hope he's great," Falcons running back Bijan Robinson about Penix, per Raimondi . "I hope that it could maybe only be just a bruise or something like that, and it just felt a little like that in the moment, but I just pray he's all right. I know the whole team does." Penix, 26, had a solid game, throwing for 240 yards and a touchdown. But on the final drive in regulation he took a big hit from Tavius Robinson and fumbled, though Atlanta managed to recover the loose ball. The game then went into overtime and the Ravens scored a touchdown on their first possession. Penix remained on the bench and was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa, who threw a pick on the second play of the drive. Penix also tore his ACL twice in college, and shoulder injuries also cost him significant time at the college level. It's been a bumpy road from a health perspective. If Penix has any sort of setback between now and kickoff, Tagovailoa could be called back into action. He was released by the Miami Dolphins ahead of the 2026 campaign after a string of disappointing seasons, though he brings plenty of experience (76 career starts) to the position.

FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. left the Atlanta Falcons' Week 5 game against the Baltimore Ravens late in the fourth quarter after taking a shot to the ribs. He returned one play later to attempt one pass on third down, but Penix did not take the field with the offense for Atlanta's only possession in overtime after a lengthy drive by Baltimore. Head coach Kevin Stefanski said that if everything goes according to plan, he expects Penix to start against the Bears in Week 6 but first wants to monitor his quarterback's injury throughout the week. With any injury like this, you want to make sure, as they move around, how they are feeling. It could be all, some, none; we shall see." Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT 3 Bold Predictions for the Browns in Week 6 against the Ravens Andrew Harbaugh, Browns Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 2:04 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns are coming off their first loss since Week 1 as they head into Week 6. They are now 3-2 and have a pivotal matchup with the Baltimore Ravens on the horizon in what has now become a must-win game for them. The Browns can only control what they can control, and in Week 6 that is going to be more important than ever. The Ravens have been dealing with several injuries, including the most notable one regarding Lamar Jackson. Whether he plays or not, this defense needs to prepare the way they know how to. On offense, Todd Monken and Deshaun Watson have to find that spark again after losing the momentum they had been building. Without doing both of those things, this could be a major setback for the season as a whole. With that said, we have our eyes on three matchups within this game that we want to highlight. Carson Schwesinger vs. Lamar Jackson Carson Schwesinger has played at an All-Pro level this year, but he is dealing with an ankle injury. Also dealing with an ankle injury is Lamar Jackson. Neither man is likely to be 100%, so who will have the willpower to overcome the other? Schwesinger has been really flashing his pass-rush presence in 2026, which will help contain Lamar Jackson, but he also has just done a tremendous job patrolling the middle of the field. He will have to be on his A game against one of the best players of this generation. Denzel Ward vs. Zay Flowers Denzel Ward is quietly having one of the best seasons of his career, just as Zay Flowers is. The Browns cornerback has allowed an average of just 20 yards to players he is covering in 2026. On the flip side, Zay Flowers is averaging 97.3 yards per game, something has to give, right? Flowers has been pretty well contained in his career against the Browns, but every matchup is a fresh start. Whoever wins this matchup between two proverbial titans could tip the scales in their team's favor. Todd Monken vs. Jessee Minter Todd Monken will be playing against the team he left to become a head coach this offseason. He is familiar with the Ravens, Lamar Jackson, Zay Flowers, and everyone on that offense, so what will he be able to do to help Mike Rutenberg and his defense? On the flip side, Jesse Minter is looking to continue the hot start to his coaching career as the Ravens themselves are sitting pretty at 4-1. These coaches seem poised to face each other for years, but the first matchup will perhaps be the most interesting. away.headline: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson unlikely to face Browns after another absence
away.blurb: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson missed the open portion of practice Friday, putting his availability for Sunday’s game against the Cleveland Browns in serious doubt. The two-time NFL Most Valuable Player has not practiced since suffering an ankle injury on Oct. 4 in a win over the Tennessee Titans. He’s considered day-to-day, but now faces the risk of missing a second straight game. Tyler “Snoop” Huntley, who led Baltimore (4-1) to a 30-23 overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, would get another start if Jackson can’t go. Huntley is 3-0 as the starter over the past two seasons and 8-9 in his career. The Ravens are 7-11 in games Jackson has missed since he became the starter in 2019. Also Friday, center Cam Jurgens (concussion), whom the Ravens traded for on Oct. 7 , and wide receiver Rashod Bateman (shoulder) wore noncontact jerseys. Tight end Matt Hibner emerged with a cast on his left hand and wearing street clothes. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley (toe/ankle) and defensive linemen Calais Campbell (rest) and Broderick Washington Jr. (ankle) also missed practice. Coach Jesse Minter is scheduled to speak to reporters after practice, and the team will release an official injury report with game statuses later this afternoon. This article will be updated. away.headline: Lamar Jackson injury: Ravens QB ‘likely’ out vs. Browns
away.blurb: Jackson, who sprained his left ankle in Baltimore’s win over the Tennessee Titans back on October 4, was not available for the media portion of practice on Friday ahead of the Ravens’ game against the Cleveland Browns this weekend. Jackson has not practiced yet this week, which is a sign that Tyler Huntley is in line to start his second game in a row: The Baltimore Ravens are “likely” to be without star quarterback Lamar Jackson for the second consecutive week. Huntley completed 8-of-9 passes for 63 yards in relief of Jackson in the early October game against the Titans, helping Baltimore salt away a 24-18 victory. Huntley got the start for the Ravens against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday night, completing 24-of-32 passes for 201 yards and a pair of touchdowns, as the Ravens won 30-23 in overtime. Huntley also started a late-season game against the Green Bay Packers a year ago, guiding Baltimore to a 41-24 victory in Lambeau Field. As noted by Ravens beat reporter Jamison Hensley above, in his last three starts for the Ravens — all wins — Huntley and the offense have averaged over 33 points. Our own Doug Farrar also named Huntley one of his “ AFC Secret Superstars ” after his performance against the Falcons.

away.headline: Major injury update for Lamar Jackson and the Ravens
away.blurb: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Jackson could be available for Sunday’s AFC North matchup against the Cleveland Browns, providing an encouraging development for a Ravens team looking to maintain its early-season momentum. “Ravens QB Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to return for Sunday’s game at Cleveland, per league source,” Schefter reported Wednesday. The update comes after Jackson suffered an ankle injury during Baltimore’s Week 4 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Jackson exited the game at halftime and did not return, leaving backup quarterback Tyler Huntley to finish the contest. The Ravens held on for a 24-18 victory, but Jackson’s injury immediately raised concerns about how long Baltimore might be without its two-time NFL MVP. Those concerns increased when Jackson missed practice the following week and was eventually ruled out against Atlanta. However, the latest report suggests his absence could be limited to just one game. “To Lamar’s credit, he’s doing everything he can to get back out there,” Minter added. “I think we’ll know more by the middle of the week.” Jackson’s potential return would be significant for a Baltimore offense that has relied heavily on his ability to create plays through the air and on the ground. Through four appearances this season, Jackson has completed 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception. Although the Ravens would welcome his return, Huntley has helped keep the team moving in his absence. His participation in practice and how his ankle responds throughout the week will likely play an important role in determining whether he can return against Cleveland. The Baltimore Ravens could be getting their starting quarterback back sooner than expected. After missing Baltimore’s Week 5 victory over the Atlanta Falcons with an ankle injury, Lamar Jackson reportedly has a realistic chance of returning to the field this weekend. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter had already offered an encouraging update Monday, explaining that Jackson was making progress in his recovery. “He’s definitely doing better,” Minter said . Minter also acknowledged that the team was still evaluating whether Jackson would be ready to participate in practice Wednesday. He has also contributed 144 rushing yards and another touchdown, continuing to provide the dual-threat production that makes him one of the NFL’s most difficult quarterbacks to defend. The veteran quarterback stepped into the starting role against Atlanta and delivered a strong performance in Baltimore’s 30-23 overtime victory. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Falcons injury report: Za'Darius Smith, Jake Matthews questionable vs. Ravens
away.blurb: Falcons injury report: Za'Darius Smith, Jake Matthews questionable vs. Ravens Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE Two other defensive starters are also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game. Atlanta's defensive front has played well to start the season, but it could be down a pair of pass rushers in this matchup. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith is questionable due to a concussion/neck injury, and linebacker Yasir Abdullah will miss the game with a hamstring injury. Editor's note: Smith was downgraded on Saturday afternoon and ruled out of this Sunday's game vs. the Ravens. On the same day, Abdullah was placed on injured reserve. Three other starters are questionable to play in the game: linebacker Divine Deablo, defensive end Samson Ebukam—both of whom are dealing with hamstring injuries—and offensive tackle Jake Matthews, who injured his groin during the Falcons' win against the New Orleans Saints on Monday night. Matthews left the game and did not return, but he has been showing progress throughout the week. Matthews was initially listed as a non-participant in Atlanta's estimated injury report on Wednesday, but he logged a limited practice on Thursday and was a full participant on Friday. That steady uptick in practice work could be taken as a positive sign that Matthews can make his 201st consecutive NFL start on Sunday night. Deablo and Ebukam were both listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the Saints, and both ended up playing and making an impact in the win. home.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Ravens QB's Status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
home.blurb: Jackson has a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game at Cleveland," ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Wednesday. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter later told reporters that Jackson is considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Bleacher Report • 9h Jalen Hurts Out Sunday Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson could be back on the field in time for a Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns. Pats Open AJ's Practice Window He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the Ravens are "hopeful" Trey Hendrickson—who has missed two games with a thumb injury—returns this week. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. A matchup with the Tennessee Titans presents an opportunity to do just that, with Indianapolis entering as the clear favorite against its division rival. But divisional games rarely follow a predictable script, and the Colts have plenty to prove as they look to build on their iffy start to the season. With another week of football ahead, here are four bold predictions for Sunday's matchup in Nashville. Red Zone Struggles Will Continue Through the first five games, the Colts red zone offense has been ultra-reliable. Indianapolis ranks eighth in the NFL in red zone scoring percentage, finding the end zone 66.7% of the time. But that efficiency took a hit in Pittsburgh.The Colts drove into the red zone on three separate occasions, but only found the end zone once. I expect those struggles to continue, despite facing a Tennessee defense that’s allowing red zone touchdowns at a 62.5% clip. The Steelers exposed the blueprint the Colts have been using by loading the defensive front with physical run stuffers and keeping gains to a minimum against the run. If the rest of the secondary does its job, and the run defense holds strong in short yardage, then it could be another long day for the Colts offense. Titans Double Scoring Average, Amplifying Questions About Colts’ Defense The Titans rank dead last in the NFL in points scored per game (11.6). The Colts defense is towards the bottom of the league in points allowed per game with 27.6, sixth-most in the NFL. The Colts defensive issues go deep, with allowing so many points being a symptom of the overall problem. Indianapolis ranks near the bottom of the league in pass rush pressure rate and has repeatedly surrendered explosive plays, which have made it difficult for the defense to stay off the field. However, I expect Indianapolis to continue struggling to generate consistent pressure, even against a vulnerable offensive line. Tennessee presents an opportunity to change that narrative after allowing four sacks against Houston last week. However, I expect Indianapolis to continue struggling to generate consistent pressure, even against a vulnerable offensive line. Arden Key is on injured reserve for at least three more weeks, and the pass rush is lacking reliable production. Without consistent pressure, the Colts will have to rely on their secondary to hold up in coverage for extended periods, giving Cam Ward more opportunities to find open receivers. If Indianapolis can't capitalize on Tennessee's protection issues, it will be another frustrating afternoon for a defense searching for answers. Colts Win, But Unconvincingly The Colts will have an opportunity to get back on track against a winless Titans team that has struggled to generate offense. However, Indianapolis cannot afford to mistake a favorable matchup for a sign that its problems have been solved. The 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh exposed recurring issues with tackling, explosive plays allowed and red-zone execution that contributed to the team's struggles. Indianapolis has yet to demonstrate that it can consistently pair its offensive production with dependable defensive play. The Colts can move the ball and put points on the board, but defensive breakdowns have made it difficult to control games when the offense fails to deliver on every possession. Tennessee offers a chance to correct that imbalance, but the Colts will need to show greater discipline and execution on defense to do so. I expect Indianapolis to come away with a win, but not necessarily the kind of complete performance that quiets concerns about the team's ability to compete with the AFC's better teams. Beating Tennessee is important for the standings. Showing tangible improvement in the areas that cost them against Pittsburgh would be far more meaningful for the Colts' long-term outlook. Gilberto Manzano correctly bet on the Green Bay Packers to upset the Chicago Bears, and yours truly bet on the San Francisco 49ers to beat the Seattle Seahawks. We move on to the Week 6 slate, and three writers have their upset picks locked in. Let's dive into them. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 6 Upset Pick Houston Texans (+120) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars First, let me pat myself on the back for finally getting an upset pick correctly. Now that I’ve regained your trust after my Packers-over-Bears pick came to fruition last week, do yourself a favor and take the new-look Texans over the London Jaguars. Houston gained confidence from beating up on Tennessee and landing wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. C.J. Stroud tends to play at his best when Nico Collins is on the field, but now he doesn’t have to lock in on him with the arrival of Harrison, who played with Stroud at Ohio State. More importantly, the Texans’ defense is back on track, and that could present trouble for the inconsistent Trevor Lawrence. Iain MacMillan Week 6 Upset Pick Tennessee Titans (+260) vs. Indianapolis Colts It's time for the Titans to get their first win of the season. You might be surprised to find out how many metrics these two teams rank similarly in, even some that the Titans outrank the Colts in, like net yards per play, which has the Titans at -0.7 and the Colts second-last in the NFL at -1.6. Another interesting metric for this game is that the Titans have the second-highest run frequency in neutral game states, meaning on early downs in the middle of the game when they still have a more than 20% win probability, Tennessee loves to run the football. That could be an area they exploit in this game, as the Colts rank dead last in the NFL in opponent rush EPA and 30th in opponent run success rate. Meanwhile, the Titans rank 16th and 11th in those two run defense categories, which will go a long way in slowing down Jonathan Taylor, which is the key to beating this Colts team. I'll take Tennessee as my upset pick of the week. Peter Dewey Week 6 Upset Pick Carolina Panthers (-105) vs. Philadelphia Eagles This isn’t the craziest upset pick in Week 6 – Carolina is just a 1.5-point underdog – but I can’t pass up a chance to fade this Philadelphia offense. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with soft-tissue injuries, and the Eagles currently rank 30th in EPA/Play, 31st in success rate and 31st in yards per play this season. Only the Tennessee Titans (0-5) are averaging fewer yards per play than Philly. I think there’s a real chance that Bryce Young and this Carolina offense (eighth in EPA/Play, sixth in EPA/Pass and fifth in yards per play) put up too many points for this Eagles team to compete. After all, the Eagles are 17th in yards per play allowed on defense and 22nd in both EPA/Play and success rate. Both of those advanced numbers are behind the Panthers’ defense this season. If the Eagles didn’t enter the season with playoff expectations, I think they’d be underdogs on Sunday based on their statistical profile in 2026. Plus, Carolina is coming off a bye while the Eagles have a tough travel week coming from London. All signs point to a Panthers upset in Week 6. picks.headline: NFL experts predict winner of Colts vs. Titans Week 6 game
picks.blurb: NFL experts predict winner of Colts vs. Titans Week 6 game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT NFL experts predict winner of Colts vs. Titans Week 6 game Paul Bretl, Colts Wire Fri, October 16, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts return home in Week 6 for a divisional matchup with the Tennessee Titans . Following last week's disappointing loss in Pittsburgh, the Colts dropped to 2-3 on the season and are in need of a win against the 0-5 Titans. But will they get it? Here is who the experts are picking to win this game. ESPN's three experts are all taking the Colts to win this game while doing so rather comfortably. ESPN's FPI prediction model also gives Indianapolis a 72.1% chance of winning this game by an average of 6.1 points. Pro Football Talk Mike Florio is picking the Colts to win 27-10. "The Colts can't afford to lose at home to a team that can't do much on either side of the ball." Pete Prisco also likes the Colts to win by multiple scores. 28-17 Indianapolis. "The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game." Almost a clean sweep. Four of the five NFL.com experts are picking the Colts to win. But Gennaro Filice likes the Titans -- here's why: "Admittedly, Tennessee has played like the most beatable team in the entire league, particularly on offense, where the Titans rank dead last in points and yards by comfortable margins. But Saleh's D at least has some bite, especially up front. Jeffery Simmons is an absolute force of nature, and while John Franklin-Myers has yet to validate his $63 million deal as a pass rusher, he remains quite effective against the run. Is it that hard to imagine the Titans containing Jonathan Taylor , getting just enough offense from Cam Ward and eking out a low-wattage win?" Nas 0728 Titans Camp 003 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Jon Spradley Mon, October 12, 2026 at 11:01 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts are picking up divisional play in Week 6 against the Tennessee Titans. It's a welcomed return home after a road trip that produced mixed results. After traveling to London and collecting a win, things went sideways in Pittsburgh. FanDuel Sportsbook is giving the Colts the edge against the winless Titans with a 6.5-point spread advantage. The money line is at -330 with the over/under starting at 43.5. The Colts did what they do; they lost in Pittsburgh. Unable to finish drives and giving up huge plays on defense was the story of the afternoon. After going up 3-0, they never regained the lead. Every time the Colts got close, they had to settle for 3. Luckily, Spencer Schrader was on his game, but it wasn't enough. An 80 and 50 yard score by Jaylen Warren was too much to overcome as the Colts fell, once again, to the Steelers in Pittsburgh. The Titans and Texans were entrenched in the battle of the winless as one team would get off the schneid and the other would sink further down. Cam Ward and the Titans might really be that bad. They scored the first 3 but then allowed the Texans to rattle off the next 26. Jobs might be on the line as the season is quickly slipping down the drain. Lose again and the Titans might be eyeing a replacement for Ward in the draft with the No. 1 pick. The Colts have work to do, but the Titans might be the best remedy to what ails them. Nothing is certain, but this is a great opportunity to get to 3-3 and finish the first third of the season at .500. Finding the end zone and putting up 6 in place of 3 is a great place to start. The Colts can do it, but they have plenty to tighten up before then.

home.headline: Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts
home.blurb: The Colts are seeking consistency at linebacker, with snaps divided in Week 5 between Akeem Davis-Gaither (52 snaps), Austin Ajiake (32 snaps), CJ Allen (24 snaps) and Bryce Boettcher (11 snaps) with starting WILL linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) out. As with Davis-Gaither, the Colts see value in Pratt's experience not only in the NFL, but with Anarumo's system. Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts signed the 30-year-old Pratt, who started 12 games for them in 2025, to their practice squad on Tuesday. While Germaine Pratt went unsigned up until Tuesday, he found a way to still be involved in football. The 30-year-old veteran linebacker spent time in the summer as a volunteer coach at North Carolina State , where he worked with his alma mater's linebackers. He eventually had a tryout with the Dallas Cowboys, though he didn't sign. This week, Pratt got his chance to get back into playing instead of coaching. The Colts signed him to their practice squad on Tuesday, and while it's too early to tell if and when he'll make his 2026 debut, Pratt said his goal is to use his experience to bring leadership to the Colts' linebacker room. "Helping the defense, just being in this system for so long, that's all I know," Pratt said. "So help it stabilize and settle it down, make tackles, whatever the case may be, get some turnovers." Pratt has played all but four of his 112 NFL games for Lou Anarumo, his defensive coordinator with the Cincinnati Bengals (2019-2024) and Colts (2025). In 2025, Pratt signed with the Colts in October after being released by the Las Vegas Raiders and started 12 games, totaling 101 tackles, a forced fumble and an interception. The experienced WILL linebacker has had over 100 tackles with at least one interception and one forced fumble every year since 2023. "Just adding a veteran presence is big in there," head coach Shane Steichen said. "He's played a lot of football in this league, made a lot of plays, and any time you can add good players to your roster, you want to do that." In the immediate future, whether Pratt could factor into that group on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans – he'd have to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad – remains to be seen given he didn't participate in training camp and took the field for his first practice of the 2026 season on Wednesday. "I don't know the plan," Pratt said. The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. With more bye weeks ahead, it’s important to save a few top teams – if possible – for a game that may not be as much of a sure thing. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. Their defense is a top 10 unit and Drake Maye can still torch a below average secondary. The Patriots now rank 10th in EPA per play, while the New York Jets rank 20th. New England is also 11th in opponent success rate, while New York is 23rd. That could all lead to big things for the Patriots in this divisional game. The Patriots have a ton of tough games on their schedule this season, including the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, so taking them when they're at home against either the Jets or Dolphins is going to be the move, which is why this is the week I'll take them at Gillette Stadium against Geno Smith and Aaron Glenn. Plus, New England is 18-2 at home in its last 20 games against the Jets. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. away.headline: Two key Browns players leave Week 5 against the Jets with injuries
away.blurb: The loss doesn't seem to be just in the standings for the Browns now, as reports come out of it that they saw both running back Quinshon Judkins and linebacker Carson Schqesinger leave in walking boots. Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot was the one to share this information after the game. On Monday, we didn't have an update on Judkins, but NFL Media's Ian Rapoport shared one on Schwesinger. He posted on social media, saying, "Browns star LB Carson Schwesinger suffered a Grade 1 ankle sprain in their loss against the Jets, though the injury occurred before his strip sack of Geno Smith, sources say. He is not ruled out for this week, though availability depends on how he responds." The idea of the Browns' defense losing Schwesinger for any amount of time would be devastating. The team has the Baltimore Ravens next up on the schedule, who are dealing with injuries of their own, but they need him for them and more.

away.headline: Jets rookie WR Cooper to play vs. Patriots; RB Hall, WR Mitchell out
away.blurb: Jets rookie WR Cooper to play vs. Patriots; RB Hall, WR Mitchell out - ABC7 New York 24/7 Live New York City New Jersey Long Island Northern Suburbs Connecticut SPORTS Share Follow abc7NY on Google FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets rookie Omar Cooper Jr ., who sustained a high ankle sprain on the first drive of the first game, will return Sunday to face the New England Patriots -- a boost to New York's injury-plagued receiving corps. Rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq , who went out with a concussion in last week's home win over the Cleveland Browns , practiced fully Friday and is "finishing up" his protocol, coach Aaron Glenn said. As expected, running back Breece Hall (quadriceps) and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) were ruled out. It will be Hall's third straight missed game, Mitchell's fourth. Mitchell underwent a surgical procedurelast month to repair an injured finger on his right hand. The Jets are hopeful that both can return next week. Left guard Dylan Parham (knee) also will miss his third straight. With Sadiq and Cooper -- both first-round picks -- the offense for this road game will be healthier than it has been in weeks, but still not whole. Cooper played only four snaps in his NFL debut, which included one dazzling play -- a 30-yard reception in which he broke several tackles against the Tennessee Titans . He was expected to be the Jets' No. 3 receiver, behind Garrett Wilson and Mitchell, but the receiving corps had to be shuffled because of injuries to Cooper, Mitchell and Tim Patrick , who returned last week from injured reserve. Cooper was a full participant Friday and will be activated from injured reserve. The Jets have an open roster spot. "It's a rookie that had a really big catch in that first Tennessee game, things that we expect from him when it comes to the catch-and-run opportunities," Glenn said. Wilson has dominated the Jets' passing attack with a team-high 31 receptions. The next closest is Sadiq (14). The Jets (2-3) haven't received much production from their second, third and fourth wideout spots since the Mitchell injury, with Patrick and Isaiah Williams , among others, in those roles. Without Hall, the Jets again will lean on Braelon Allen , who rushed for a career-high 116 yards last week. "We think we have the best one-two combination in the NFL," offensive coordinator Frank Reich said. On defense, they will be without edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle), who will miss his third game. away.headline: Patriots Get Double Injury Boost as Jets Rule Out 2 Weapons
away.blurb: Patriots Get Double Injury Boost as Jets Rule Out 2 Weapons The New York Jets have ruled out running back Breece Hall and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell for their Week 6 matchup against New England, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Friday. Hall is dealing with a quadriceps injury, while Mitchell stats sidelined with a finger injury. Both players failed to practice Wednesday and Thursday before being officially ruled out. The 25-year-old opened the season as New York's lead back, carrying 51 times for 163 yards and a touchdown through three appearances. He also caught 10 passes for 102 yards, giving quarterback Geno Smith receiving help out of the backfield. New England has its own lengthy injury report, including cornerback Carlton Davis III missing the first two practices of the week with a neck injury. There was good news elsewhere, though, as Christian Gonzalez progressed from limited Wednesday to a full participant Thursday. Unlock the latest Heavy on Patriots news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 16, 2026 at 11:24am The New England Patriots will catch another break on the injury front when they meet an AFC East rival on Sunday. The absences take two explosive options away from a Jets offense that ranks near the bottom of the NFL . New York averages 284 yards per game, 26th in the league, and 18.6 points per contest. New England, meanwhile, owns the NFL's fifth-ranked total defense at 296.2 yards allowed per game. Hall Absence Changes Jets' Backfield Getty EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY – SEPTEMBER 20: Breece Hall #20 of the New York Jets runs with the ball against the Green Bay Packers during the first half of the game at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) Hall will miss his third consecutive game after suffering the quad injury against the Detroit Lions on Sept. 27. His absence doesn't mean the Patriots can overlook the Jets' running game. Braelon Allen has taken advantage of the increased workload. The former Wisconsin standout rushed 24 times for 116 yards and a touchdown in New York's 17-12 win over the Cleveland Browns last week. He has totaled 175 rushing yards on 38 carries over his two starts since Hall went down. That sets up an eye-catching matchup against one of New England's strongest units.
