away.headline: New York Jets get some reinforcements for New England Patriots game
away.blurb: Both rookies fully practiced on Friday and appear ready to go. Sadiq was earlier listed as questionable with concussion symptoms, but apparently has passed the NFL protocols. Cooper was on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain They will be needed against the 3-2 Patriots. Once again, No. 2 receiver Adonai Mitchell and star running back Breece Hall will not play. Left guard Dylan Parham is also out, as is defensive edge Joseph Ossai, who has apparently reaggravated his foot injury. Mitchell has since undergone what the Jets have described as a “procedure” on his hand after denying at first that such action had been taken. However, he is still week-to-week, and it’s anyone’s guess as to when he might possibly return. Parham’s knee injury is also a bit of a mystery. He was seen walking around the Jets facility in an air cast, but has not been placed on injured reserve. Big men and knees are tricky, so when he will be ready to return is up in the air. His replacement, Jordan Meredith, has been struggling, yielding three sacks and ten total pressures. Cooper’s return offers intrigue on whether he can provide a deep threat to take the heat off No. 1 receiver Garrett Wilson. Cooper had a 30-yard catch and run on opening day against the Tennessee Titans, pinballing down the field and opening some eyes as to his potential. If he can make a play or two in a limited role, it opens up the field for the other Jets weapons. Sadiq had a big game against the Detroit Lions, winning the NFL Rookie of the Week award. He has since been limited, but his blazing speed always poses a threat that can open things up for others. He joins the returned Mason Taylor as a 1-2 punch at tight end. The New York Jets will likely have tight end Kenyon Sadiq and wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. in their game against the New England Patriots on Sunday. Of the missing, Mitchell is the most concerning. He will miss his fourth straight game after sustaining a finger injury at a Jets practice. He allegedly caught his finger in a teammate’s jersey, an unfortunate accident that has derailed a promising start to his season. Hall’s quad injury has been slow-healing, but the muscle is one that running backs need to be perfect in order to perform. He will miss his third straight game. In his absence, Braelon Hall has come on strong, rushing for more than 100 yards in his last game and scoring an impressive touchdown run to seal a Jets victory over the Cleveland Browns.

home.headline: Jets rookie WR Cooper to play vs. Patriots; RB Hall, WR Mitchell out
home.blurb: Jets rookie WR Cooper to play vs. Patriots; RB Hall, WR Mitchell out - ABC7 New York 24/7 Live New York City New Jersey Long Island Northern Suburbs Connecticut SPORTS Share Follow abc7NY on Google FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets rookie Omar Cooper Jr ., who sustained a high ankle sprain on the first drive of the first game, will return Sunday to face the New England Patriots -- a boost to New York's injury-plagued receiving corps. Rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq , who went out with a concussion in last week's home win over the Cleveland Browns , practiced fully Friday and is "finishing up" his protocol, coach Aaron Glenn said. As expected, running back Breece Hall (quadriceps) and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) were ruled out. It will be Hall's third straight missed game, Mitchell's fourth. Mitchell underwent a surgical procedurelast month to repair an injured finger on his right hand. The Jets are hopeful that both can return next week. Left guard Dylan Parham (knee) also will miss his third straight. With Sadiq and Cooper -- both first-round picks -- the offense for this road game will be healthier than it has been in weeks, but still not whole. Cooper played only four snaps in his NFL debut, which included one dazzling play -- a 30-yard reception in which he broke several tackles against the Tennessee Titans . He was expected to be the Jets' No. 3 receiver, behind Garrett Wilson and Mitchell, but the receiving corps had to be shuffled because of injuries to Cooper, Mitchell and Tim Patrick , who returned last week from injured reserve. Cooper was a full participant Friday and will be activated from injured reserve. The Jets have an open roster spot. "It's a rookie that had a really big catch in that first Tennessee game, things that we expect from him when it comes to the catch-and-run opportunities," Glenn said. Wilson has dominated the Jets' passing attack with a team-high 31 receptions. The next closest is Sadiq (14). The Jets (2-3) haven't received much production from their second, third and fourth wideout spots since the Mitchell injury, with Patrick and Isaiah Williams , among others, in those roles. Without Hall, the Jets again will lean on Braelon Allen , who rushed for a career-high 116 yards last week. "We think we have the best one-two combination in the NFL," offensive coordinator Frank Reich said. On defense, they will be without edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle), who will miss his third game. The Giants tied with the Washington Commanders in what ended up being one of the weirder games of the season. New York should have lost to Washington, so the fact that they tied is being taken as a win for the team. But the Giants know that they will need a better effort going forward this week as the team gets ready to face off against the New Orleans Saints at home. New Orleans will be coming into the game looking to stop the bleeding, with the Saints sitting with a record of 1-4 on the year. Both sides need a win this week for different reasons, and the Giants will try to remain perfect at home this season. New York can't overlook this Saints team despite their struggles this season; otherwise, the Giants could find themselves in a tight contest. Bleacher Report did game predictions for every contest this week, with Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford picking. In these predictions, every single expert went with the Giants to take down New Orleans. Much of this could be due to the Saints having their own problems this year, but the Giants have shown real promise as a team. Even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart going down with an injury, the Giants have been able to stay the course. Backup signal-caller Jameis Winston has held down the fort well for New York, showing that he can get this team to the playoffs. But the problem with Winston is that he has been very inconsistent over the years in his career, and the Giants know this from the first few weeks of the season. As he gets ready to face off against New Orleans, Winston will need to make sure to stay focused. Winston can be very turnover-prone at times, and the Giants can't afford any issues against the Saints this week. The Giants defense has been a calling card for the team this season, helping them win a few games. And going against an explosive Saints passing attack, the New York secondary will need to be ready to go. The kickoff for the game between the Giants and Saints is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey

away.blurb: Saints vs. Giants: Jameis Winston's Return Headlines 3 Key Storylines Skip to main content SI.COM The New Orleans Saints enter Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants looking to avoid their fourth consecutive loss, but a familiar face stands in their way and remains a fan favorite in New Orleans. Former Saints quarterback Jameis Winston will lead the Giants against his former team as New Orleans attempts to rebound from a disappointing 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . The Saints (1-4) have struggled to find consistency on both sides of the football, particularly offensively, where turnovers and an ineffective passing attack have contributed to their disappointing start. Meanwhile, the Giants (3-1-1) have emerged as one of the NFC's early surprises under first-year coach John Harbaugh, overcoming injuries and inconsistent quarterback play to remain atop the NFC East. Beyond Winston's reunion with New Orleans, the Saints must contend with two dangerous receiving threats in Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely while finding a way to exploit New York's ball-security problems. Here are three major storylines to watch heading into Sunday's matchup. Winston, a fan favorite among Who Dat Nation, will be the starter against his former team. The former No. 1 overall pick spent four seasons with the Saints from 2020-23, initially serving as Drew Brees ' backup before becoming New Orleans' starting quarterback in 2021. Now, Winston has the chance to face his former team while trying to keep the Giants atop the NFC East. Winston became the starter after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury. Through three starts this season, Winston has thrown for 805 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions while completing 57.6% of his passes. In his latest outing against Washington, Winston helped engineer the comeback by completing 33 of his 54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns, connecting twice with Isaiah Likely and once with Malik Nabers . Perhaps most importantly, Winston avoided throwing an interception despite attempting 54 passes. Can the Saints Slow Down Malik Nabers and Isiah Likely? While Winston commands attention, the Saints' biggest defensive challenge may be containing his top targets, wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely. Nabers (29 catches for 329 yards and two touchdowns) and Likely (33 catches for 284 yards and four touchdowns) are responsible for 58% of the yardage production and number of targets thrown to. Nabers, a former LSU star, has bounced back from a season-ending knee injury. He caught six passes for 112 yards and a touchdown against Arizona in Week 4, then recorded 11 catches for 121 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets against Washington. away.headline: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve
away.blurb: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve Welcome back, Zach Wood. The New Orleans Saints long snapper was a full participant at practice on Wednesday, marking his return from injured reserve. He'll need to continue practicing throughout the week in order to be activated for Sunday's game with the New York Giants , but all signs point to him snapping the ball at MetLife Stadium. The Saints released fill-in long snapper Cal Adomitis and don't have another player at the position on their roster. They also left a vacancy open and waiting for Wood on the 53-man roster once he gets the green light. Wood, 33, won the job back in 2017 and was the long snapper for New Orleans in 150 consecutive regular season games (plus seven playoff games), finally ending his streak when a calf strain forced him out of action the last four weeks. The fear was that he would have needed even more time to recover, but he's ahead of schedule and expected to be back in the lineup. Wood has made quite a career for himself as a former rookie free agent out of SMU. He actually spent some time with the Dallas Cowboys when Kellen Moore was the backup quarterback in 2016 and part of the 2017 preseason. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: New Orleans Saints 150-game starter begins return from injured reserve John Sigler, Saints Wire Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:56 AM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads He's been missed. Adomitis had some hiccups and drew an untimely penalty during Week 5's loss to the Minnesota Vikings , so getting Wood back on the field should help steady the operation. You just hope he isn't rushing himself back too soon.

away.headline: Vikings-Saints Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, some intrigue with a number of players listed as questionable, including Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson, and Brian O’Neill. I’m gonna go out on a limb and say that all three will play on Sunday. I know they will be cautious with all of them, but it doesn’t sound like Jefferson has experienced any problems with his ankle all week. It sounds like Addison and O’Neill’s injuries are more of the minor variety they will play through. It’s not a surprise at this point that Christian Darrisaw is out, as he hadn’t practiced all week. He should be ready to go after the bye week. For the Saints, Alvin Kamara is questionable but my guess is he’ll play on Sunday. Safety Julian Blackmon is also questionable but probably will play as well. Those are the two key players on the Saints list this week. Everyone else is either listed as out or do not have a deisignation and/or are a backup. Who will be sitting this one out? home.headline: With Jalen Hurts’ injury revealed, this NY Giants fan is rooting for his speedy recovery
home.blurb: After being “cleated” in last week’s game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the former Super Bowl MVP complained to the Eagles’ medical staff about calf pain. The Eagles said that, “out of an abundance of caution,” they performed an ultrasound on the area of pain. The ultrasound found a blood clot, which caused Hurts to miss this week’s match-up in London against the Carolina Panthers. The phrase “this ain’t ballet” comes to mind whenever you see or hear of an injury in the NFL . Unfortunately, the injury bug has hit the Philadelphia Eagles in the form of Jalen Hurts ‘ superficial blood clot. As a resident New York Giants fan, I still hate to see Hurts go down. He’s one of us . It has been reported that the Eagles staff knew of this ailment before the Eagles’ trip across the pond. If so, there certainly is some negligence involved in putting Hurts at risk, having a blood clot, and getting on a flight. Future contract extension implications do exist. But Hurts’ health is paramount right now. Currently, the Eagles sit at 2-3 for the season. It’s been a tale of two seasons so far: the Eagles started with a two-game winning streak. Since then, they’ve been on a three-game schneid. One could think that this injury couldn’t come at a worse time. Even though the Eagles are my rivals, I actually see things differently. I much rather have injuries happen earlier in the season rather than late. With only week six and 11 weeks left, the Eagles may not be in any peril. As of now, reports say Hurts will only miss week six. As an eternal optimist, I think that with a week off, the Eagles’ franchise player could be back for week 7. In fact, I’m pretty sure that’s his goal, if he has anything to do with it. It allows Hurts to rest and heal for almost two weeks. As for week nine? Well, the Eagles land in the Meadowlands to face Big Blue! As the competitor that I am, I want to play the birds at their best; it helps for all of the bragging rights. I want no caveats. I want to beat the Hurts-led Philadelphia Eagles on our field! So I want Hurts suited up and taking the field. As division rivals, we need a win over these guys. Thus far, with Jameis Winston at the helm, the Giants are 3-1-1. With their starting quarterback, Jaxon Dart, hurt for the season, we’ve experienced a bit more ease than the Eagles thus far. This record is so much better than where we were a year ago. But I still root for Hurts the person. I root for his recovery because, in a league like the NFL, very few players have the physical and mental deftness he has on and off the field. He’s a great example of how we succeed in the league . If for no other reason, we need to wish Hurts the best on that front alone. My message for Eagles fans is simple: Get ready for week seven, because your MVP is. Hurts will be back, prepped and focused. He wouldn’t dare take the field if he couldn’t go full throttle. So when he does, make sure you all keep those Eagles flying….that’s of course until you guys pull up

home.headline: NY Giants injury report: Abdul Carter held out of practice for 2nd straight day
home.blurb: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin), right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and edge defender Abdul Carter (calf) all worked on the side with trainers Thursday during the media viewing portion of New York Giants practice. All three, along with cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) and safety Tyler Nubin (neck) were officially listed as “did not practice.” Linebacker Malik Harrison, who was just added to the 53-man roster this week, was added to the injury report with a groin issue. He was a limited participant. For Thomas, who has been managing his injury since Week 2 against the Los Angeles Rams, this has been his weekly routine. He has yet to miss a snap due to the injury. If Carter is not able to play Sunday against the New Orleans Saints, that would be a massive blow to a Giants’ defense already without star edge defender Brian Burns (torn ACL) for the season. Carter has 2.0 sacks, and is tied sixth in the NFL among edge defenders and linebackers with 14 quarterback pressures. Carter leads the league with 11 ‘quick’ quarterback pressures, defined as pressures achieved in less than 2.5 seconds. If Eluemunor cannot play, Marcus Mbow would start at right tackle and rookie J.C. Davis would be the swing tackle. Safety Jason Pinnock, who missed last week’s game due to a concussion, was a full practice participant. That is good news, especially with Nubin trending toward not playing.

home.headline: Saints vs. Giants: Jameis Winston's Return Headlines 3 Key Storylines
home.blurb: Saints vs. Giants: Jameis Winston's Return Headlines 3 Key Storylines Skip to main content SI.COM The New Orleans Saints enter Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants looking to avoid their fourth consecutive loss, but a familiar face stands in their way and remains a fan favorite in New Orleans. Former Saints quarterback Jameis Winston will lead the Giants against his former team as New Orleans attempts to rebound from a disappointing 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . The Saints (1-4) have struggled to find consistency on both sides of the football, particularly offensively, where turnovers and an ineffective passing attack have contributed to their disappointing start. Meanwhile, the Giants (3-1-1) have emerged as one of the NFC's early surprises under first-year coach John Harbaugh, overcoming injuries and inconsistent quarterback play to remain atop the NFC East. Beyond Winston's reunion with New Orleans, the Saints must contend with two dangerous receiving threats in Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely while finding a way to exploit New York's ball-security problems. Here are three major storylines to watch heading into Sunday's matchup. Winston, a fan favorite among Who Dat Nation, will be the starter against his former team. The former No. 1 overall pick spent four seasons with the Saints from 2020-23, initially serving as Drew Brees ' backup before becoming New Orleans' starting quarterback in 2021. Now, Winston has the chance to face his former team while trying to keep the Giants atop the NFC East. Winston became the starter after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury. Through three starts this season, Winston has thrown for 805 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions while completing 57.6% of his passes. In his latest outing against Washington, Winston helped engineer the comeback by completing 33 of his 54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns, connecting twice with Isaiah Likely and once with Malik Nabers . Perhaps most importantly, Winston avoided throwing an interception despite attempting 54 passes. Can the Saints Slow Down Malik Nabers and Isiah Likely? While Winston commands attention, the Saints' biggest defensive challenge may be containing his top targets, wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely. Nabers (29 catches for 329 yards and two touchdowns) and Likely (33 catches for 284 yards and four touchdowns) are responsible for 58% of the yardage production and number of targets thrown to. Nabers, a former LSU star, has bounced back from a season-ending knee injury. He caught six passes for 112 yards and a touchdown against Arizona in Week 4, then recorded 11 catches for 121 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets against Washington. Focusing solely on Nabers, opens opportunities for Likely, a former Baltimore Raven who has become Winston's primary red-zone threat. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. The Philadelphia Eagles made the long trek back from London after a mindboggling, crushing defeat where victory was essentially secured. The Panthers have the advantage this week, it seems. Despite that, they're not favored on the road, and some experts aren't willing to pick the Panthers to take the Eagles down. CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. "The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense," he wrote. His CBS colleague, Jordan Dajani, disagreed, picking the Panthers to win 23-21. "The Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. home.blurb: Milton was a sixth-round pick by the New England Patriots in the 2024 NFL draft out of the University of Tennessee. He also played for the University of Michigan in college. Hurts was ruled out for Week 6 vs. the Carolina Panthers on Thursday with a superficial blood clot. The follow-up ultrasound showed movement in the blood clot, which led to Hurts being ruled out. Hurts' return to the field is unclear as the Eagles deal with a long list of injuries to key players, including DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley. McKee is set to start against the Panthers Sunday with Hurts out. One day after losing Jalen Hurts to a superficial blood clot, the Philadelphia Eagles signed quarterback Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad, according to multiple reports Friday. Signing Milton adds depth to Philadelphia's quarterback room behind Tanner McKee and Cole Payton with Hurts sidelined. Milton was traded to the Dallas Cowboys before the 2025 season. He's played in five games in his NFL career, including four with the Cowboys. Milton has completed 37 of his 53 passes for two touchdowns and two interceptions in five games. The Eagles said Hurts was cleated in Week 4 vs. the Los Angeles Rams, but he continued to practice fully, including popping up on the injury report with a calf injury last week. After traveling to London, Hurts underwent an ultrasound, which revealed a small blood clot. He was cleared to play by doctors against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. However, the doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound in Philly. "His health and safety are our highest priority," the team said.

picks.blurb: Analyst Predicts Steelers to Dominate Buccaneers in Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT Analyst Predicts Steelers to Dominate Buccaneers in Week 6 Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026 -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Aaron Becker Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:38 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A NFL analyst is all in on the Pittsburgh Steelers for Week 6. The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point favorites for their Week 6 road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, NFL analyst Conor Orr thinks the oddsmakers have it completely wrong. Orr predicts the Steelers will continue their hot streak and dominate the Buccaneers in Week 6. "I wanna see the Steelers go down to Tampa Bay and win another one of these games," Orr said . "I think they can win this game by three touchdowns." Orr has done a complete 180 in just a matter of a week. Heading into Week 5, he begged the Indianapolis Colts to put the Steelers out of their misery. "Clearly you have communication issues. Your coach came out and said your house is dirty and you need to clean your house. Something's a mess here," Orr said on the Heed the Call NFL Podcast . "I'm sick of [Aaron Rodgers]. I'm sick of watching this team. I'm sick of the receivers dropping balls. I'm sick of them having played one good game against the Bengals so we've got to take them seriously for another three weeks. Come on, Jonathan Taylor. Put up 400 yards and put his old, dying horse out of its misery and off my screen." However, after watching the Steelers offense come alive in their latest win, Orr issued an apology to the team and now seems to be a big believer in Pittsburgh. "I have totally done a 180, and I'll admit it, on this Steelers offense," Orr continued. "Down so many people, and even down to Ben Skowronek, this team has been able to find a way to manufacture points. Aaron Rodgers will have bad Rodgers games, but I've totally flipped on this." The Steelers do seem to have some new found life. Rodgers is playing very well and running back Jaylen Warren has been on another level, recording 176, 126 and 188-yard performances the past three weeks. The only question that remains is: Can the Steelers offense continue this type of production the rest of the season? picks.headline: Steelers-Buccaneers preview: What to expect from Tampa Bay’s offense, defense in Week 6
picks.blurb: Steelers-Buccaneers preview: What to expect from Tampa Bay’s offense, defense in Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images Ryan Parish Fri, October 16, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 12 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The 3-2 Steelers will travel to Tampa Bay in Week 6 to take on the Buccaneers, who sit at a disappointing 1-4 but are coming off their lone win of the season thus far — a 24-16 showing against the Cowboys in Week 5. It's been a rough season for Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles and co., and the team's recent three-year, $165 million extension for quarterback Baker Mayfield already isn't aging that well: The veteran passer struggled in a winless start to the year before missing games with a dislocated thumb on this throwing hand. But coming off a Thursday Night Football win in Dallas, the Buccaneers have some momentum and extra prep time to prepare for the Steelers. What should Pittsburgh expect on Sunday? What to expect from the Bucs' offense Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images | Getty Images Rushing YPG: 133 (7th) Passing YPG: 173.4 (27th) PPG: 20 (25th) RB : The Buccaneers offense will be without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for yet another game, meaning undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will once again start under center for Tampa Bay against Pittsburgh. The good news is that Daniels is a rookie with just two starts under his belt. That can show in his play and the Steelers should be able to take advantage of some mistakes on Sunday. That said, Mayfield was having a rough start to 2026, and it was Daniels who helped lead the Buccaneers to their first win of the season last week. Like everything in the NFL, beating the Buccaneers won't be slam dunk in Week 6. Daniels looked impressively poised and accurate against the Cowboys defense last week, passing for 189 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions with 76% completion. Of course, offensive coordinator Zac Robinson put together a game plan to help the young passer succeed, with an emphasis on the quick game and play action. Daniels is on the shorter side for an NFL passer (6'0), and his arm strength doesn't leap off the screen, but he drives the ball well on short and intermediate passes and only had a few rough misses against the Cowboys (note this was against a struggling Dallas defense). His escapability is an upgrade over Mayfield's, with Daniels already having 87 yards and four first downs on the ground this season. While the Buccaneers are largely a short-game passing attack, Daniels still has moments where his processing slows down and he attempts to play hero ball. Tampa Bay has a strong offensive line but currently has the third-worst sack rate in the NFL (10.1%), with 17 sacks allowed this season. A number of those plays have been quarterback error — Tampa Bay has the NFL's seventh-longest time to throw at 2.98 seconds — even if Daniels has been an improvement in that area over Mayfield. If the Steelers can keep up with Daniels in the backfield, they should be able to log some sacks or at least a handful of pressures on Sunday. But Tampa Bay's offensive line won't make that task easy. Led by one of the league's best tackles in Tristian Wirfs and a slew of other good players such as Graham Barton and Luke Goedeke, the Buccaneers can both pass protect well and maul in the run game. On the ground, the Tampa holds defenses to the sixth-lowest run stuff rate (12.5%) in the NFL. The Buccaneers are also second-best in yards before contact per attempt (2.16), per NFL Pro. The Buccaneers use a lot of motion to try to confuse defenses pre-snap, and it melds well with a rushing offense that favors gap concepts. At running back, the room has two solid names in starter Bucky Irving and former Steeler Kenny Gainwell. Both are slimmer running backs who can be a weapon in the passing game, with Irving showing off his phone-booth quickness with a long run against Dallas last week. If healthy, Sean Tucker is another name to keep an eye on in Tampa Bay's backfield as a more hard-nosed, downhill runner. At pass catcher, the Buccaneers have a number of recognizable names, but still lack an established WR1. Emeka Egbuka leads the team in receiving yards with 192 through five games, averaging just 9.1 yards per reception as a primarily underneath target. Tight end Cade Otton, with 182 yards, has also been a steady contributor. Chris Godwin Jr. hasn't had his pre-injury production, but has been another solid name in the short game with 129 of his 179 yards this season coming after the catch. On more downfield passes, 5'10 speed threat Tez Johnson averages 27.6 yards per catch on five receptions this season, while rookie Ted Hurst III, one of my favorite mid-round prospects this spring, has made some plays with eight grabs for 128 yards and a touchdown this season. Tampa Bay is one of the most 11 personnel-heavy offenses in the league, getting a wide range of receivers involved. Still, its running game ranks top 10 thanks to a competent offensive line. On paper, the Steelers' defense certainly has the talent to shut down the Buccaneers' offense, but Daniels is a bit of an X factor. Will an experienced pass rush with more film on the rookie dominate, or will Daniels continue to improve and clean up Tampa Bay's sack rate with his mobility? Also complicating things is the tendency for offensive coordinators to mix up their tendencies more when playing with a reserve quarterback. However, if the Steelers can disrupt the Buccaneers' quick passing game and run game and force Daniels to play out of rhythm and with more downfield shots, this game could bode well for the Pittsburgh defense. What to expect from the Bucs ' defense (Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Rushing YPG Allowed: 72.8 (2nd) Passing YPG Allowed: 226.6 (20th) PPG Allowed: 22.4 (T-14th) RP : The Buccaneers' defense makes a fascinating matchup for the Steelers' offense. This contest will pit strength against strength: Pittsburgh's running game versus Tampa Bay's run defense. But it will also feature weakness against weakness: the Steelers have struggled against man coverage, yet the Buccaneers run man concepts at a bottom-third rate in the league. In most metrics, the Buccaneers' run defense is near the top of the league, and their overall strategy is pretty apparent. Tampa Bay has light boxes — six or fewer defenders — at the second-lowest rate (20.7%) in the NFL. They have stacked boxes — eight or more defenders — at the second-highest rate (41.4%) in the league. Put another way, 79.3% of the time, the Bucs have seven defenders or more in the box against the run, giving them a numbers advantage if the offense doesn't answer with some combination of two tight ends, a fullback, or a condensed formation that hugs the receivers tight to their linemen. The results have followed. Not only are the Buccaneers allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game, but they're also top-seven or better in: Average yards after contact (1.72, 1st) Yards per carry (3.3, T-2nd) EPA/Rush (-0.18, 4th) Runs of 10+ yards allowed (9, T-4th) Run stuff rate (18.9%, 7th) While he doesn't fill up the stat sheet, plenty of credit for the Buccaneers' success against the run should be paid to nose tackle Vita Vea. The Bucs also find creative ways to get their linebackers and defensive backs in good position to make stops. Safety Tykee Smith and rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter currently lead the team in run stuffs with four apiece. Tampa Bay's commitment to stopping the run bleeds into what coverages they run. They live in single-high safety looks, running Cover-1 (12.9%) and Cover-3 (51.7%) a combined 64.6% of the time. Against the pass, Tampa is a mostly middling group. As a pass rush unit, they actually track well at creating pressure, but they struggle to pay it off. The Bucs have the second-quickest average time to create pressure (2.45 seconds), and opposing quarterbacks' average time to throw (2.59 seconds) is the quickest mark in the NFL. While that sounds like it should be paired with a lethal pass rush, in practice it just means opposing teams know they should attack the blitz-happy Todd Bowles defense with a quick passing attack. The Bucs blitz 41.3% of the time, the third most in the league. Despite this, they have just six sacks (28th), 55 pressures (T-26th), and a 30.7% pressure rate (29th) this season. Pair this info together, and that tells me the Steelers and quarterback Aaron Rodgers shouldn't feel like they have the freedom to hold onto the ball forever, but they should be able to exploit the defense if they're smart and playing on time. With Tampa Bay running a lot of Cover-3, the areas the Steelers should attack match well with the personnel they have available to them. Cover-3 features three deep defenders, typically a safety in the deep middle of the field, and two cornerbacks on the outside. That leaves four defenders underneath to play the flats, middle of the field, and intermediate boundary. Ways to attack this coverage include: Attacking the seam (great for TEs or slot receivers) Concepts like Flood, Sail, and Levels, which stress the underneath defenders by sending multiple pass catchers at them at different depths, forcing them to commit to one and creating an opening for the other Slants and other quick game passing concepts that can get behind the underneath defenders quickly While the Bucs have a decent mark in EPA/pass at -0.08 (12th), they are far worse in other metrics. They allow 6.6 yards per pass play (23rd) and struggle to stop pass catchers from creating after the catch. They've allowed 647 yards after the catch (29th), and +103 YAC over expectation. Zyon McCollum, Jacob Parrish, and rookie nickel Keionte Scott are taking most of their snaps at cornerback, with Benjamin Morrison missing each of the last two games with injury. Parrish is the only CB on the team with an interception (1). McCollum is having a solid season so far, with decent marks in coverage EPA (-5.3), passer rating allowed (68.8), but he has just three career interceptions, and nearly half of his career PBUs came two seasons ago. He's also got an absurdly high missed tackle rate (25%) this season, due largely to a poor game against Green Bay where he missed four tackles. Parrish is their most targeted defensive back (30) and has allowed 18 receptions for 236 yards, but he's added 5 PBUs and has just one missed tackle this season. Scott, the rookie, has struggled in coverage, allowing 14 receptions on 18 targets. His missed-tackle rate is 18.5%, with one missed tackle in each game. At safety, the Bucs will likely be without Antoine Winfield Jr. for a second straight game as he has yet to participate in practice this week while recovering from a rib injury. Ifeatu Melifonwu will be the next man up. He was only targeted twice last week, allowing one catch for 15 yards, and also adding a missed tackle. Smith, for as good as he is against the run, has been a liability against the pass, surrendering three touchdowns and an opposing passer rating of 135.3 when targeted. Linebackers Trotter and Alex Anzalone are also gettable, as they've combined to allow 28 of 36 targets to be completed for 316 yards and a score. Both do have an interception, however. Overall, this should be a winnable game for the Steelers offense. They may not find the same s

away.headline: Report: Steelers WR Roman Wilson (finger) to miss multiple weeks
away.blurb: Wilson had no catches on one target before exiting in the second quarter of the 34-22 win. He was grabbing his left hand after an incompletion and did not return to the game. ESPN reported that Wilson is still gathering more information about the injury and will seek a second opinion. Wilson, a third-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft by Pittsburgh, has 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns in five games this season. The 25-year-old has 26 receptions for 354 yards and four TDs over the last two seasons for the Steelers. Wilson’s status comes after Pittsburgh placed wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on injured reserve Saturday and Ben Skowronek also left Sunday’s game with a calf injury. away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he’s caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who’s handled a heavy workload in Dowdle’s absence. First-year coach Mike McCarthy’s team will play four of its next five games on the road starting this week, and it will take multiple longer – and daunting – trips to do so before things begin to moderate in the back half of the 2026 schedule. All of it will unfold amid mounting absences. Running back Rico Dowdle; receivers Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek; and defensive backs Jamel Dean and Jalen Ramsey have all been hurt in some form or fashion recently. The stretch will be one of, if not the, most grueling in the franchise’s history and could determine whether the Steelers ’ 3-2 start has legs, or whether another mediocre year awaits a franchise that hasn’t won an NFL playoff game since 2017. NFL Week 6 brings a road trip to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers . That’s a 1,000-or-so-mile trip right off the bat against a desperate 1-4 team that needs a win to preserve any postseason hopes. One week later, the Steelers will board a long flight to Paris to face the New Orleans Saints in the first NFL regular season game in France. It will be only the second international game for Pittsburgh since 2013. It picked up a win against Minnesota in Dublin, Ireland last October, but the travel schedule was much kinder surrounding that date. The Steelers got to enjoy a bye after their trip to the Emerald Isle and did not need to travel any further than Massachusetts until they visited the Los Angeles Chargers in early November. It was a similar story when they played in London13 years ago. They came home to a bye, and most travel was relatively local for the month before and after. Los Angeles enters the game at 2-3 after a heartbreaking 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. Arizona is 1-4 and coming off a disappointing 45-21 defeat against the Detroit Lions. Both teams need a strong performance, making Sunday's divisional matchup an important opportunity to build momentum. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. Matthew Stafford Leads the Rams Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford will be a major factor in Sunday's game as Los Angeles looks to rebound from its difficult loss to Buffalo. Stafford has thrown for 1,572 yards and nine touchdowns through five games, establishing himself as the centerpiece of an offense capable of producing explosive plays. However, six interceptions have created problems, and protecting the football will be important against Arizona. Head coach Sean McVay will look to get the offense back on track by utilizing his talented group of playmakers. Wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams give Stafford two dangerous options in the passing game, while running back Kyren Williams provides balance on the ground. Williams has recorded 343 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns, making him an important part of Los Angeles' offensive attack. The Rams will also need to adjust along the offensive line, with left tackle Alaric Jackson suspended for Sunday's matchup. Jacoby Brissett Looks to Keep Arizona Competitive Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett will lead the Cardinals as they attempt to bounce back from their loss to Detroit. Brissett has thrown for 1,110 yards and nine touchdowns this season. Despite Arizona's struggles, he has shown the ability to move the football through the air and keep the offense competitive. Tight end Trey McBride remains one of his most reliable targets, entering the matchup with 42 receptions for 308 yards and three touchdowns. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love has also contributed to Arizona's offense, although his availability and workload will be worth monitoring after he missed practice Wednesday with an ankle issue. First-year head coach Mike LaFleur will need his offense to produce consistently against a Rams defense looking to force turnovers and create pressure. A Crucial NFC West Matchup Sunday's game gives Los Angeles an opportunity to recover from its overtime defeat and improve its record. Arizona needs a stronger defensive performance after allowing 45 points against Detroit. With Stafford leading an explosive passing attack and Brissett looking to keep the Cardinals competitive, both quarterbacks will face important challenges. The Rams and Cardinals have plenty to prove, and Sunday's matchup could be an important moment for both teams as the NFC West race continues.

picks.headline: Cardinals at Rams: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 6 game
picks.blurb: Opening lines: Spread: Rams -13.5 Moneyline: Rams -750; Cardinals +13.5 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Rams vs Cardinals expert picks Adam Kaufman: Rams 34, Cardinals 20 The Rams need a get-right game. Conveniently, the Cardinals are coming to town. Los Angeles has spent enough time trading punches with contenders. Now Matthew Stafford gets an Arizona defense that should provide a much friendlier afternoon, even with the shortened turnaround after Monday night. The Cardinals can move the ball through Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, and Jeremiyah Love gives the offense a reason to stay patient. I just don't see enough defensive resistance to keep the Rams from eventually creating separation, especially after the way they fell to the Bills . The concern is asking Los Angeles to cover a huge number after an overtime game. Winning this matchup feels considerably more straightforward. Give me Stafford, Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Kyren Williams and enough explosive plays to put the Rams back in the win column. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Rams 38, Cardinals 20 Watch out, Arizona. The Rams might take out the frustrations of a 2-3 start on their divisional foe. The Cardinals haven't proven nearly capable of offering any resistance to an attack with as much firepower as Los Angeles, let alone stopping one. Maybe this isn't the game in which Carson Beck will make his NFL debut for Arizona as he looks to take on a role as more than a mere emergency quarterback, but a blowout might bring that possibility closer to reality. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Rams 31, Cardinals 16 Perhaps the Rams aren't the super team that we thought. A 2-3 start to the season certainly isn't doing the team any favors. However, Matthew Stafford looked like a quarterback that started to find himself again in Week 5 against the Bills. The Cardinals are the get-right team for every NFC West team that feels down about themselves. That's just the reality of being the doormat in a loaded division. Sean McVay's crew takes out all their frustrations on the lowly Cardinals, winning by a big margin to cover up all the special teams mistakes. away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. away.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Chiefs bold predictions for AFC West clash in Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT Chargers vs. Chiefs bold predictions for AFC West clash in Week 6 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 6:55 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Chargers visit the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday with their seasons moving in opposite directions. Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Kansas City, but divisional familiarity and turnovers can make a comfortable matchup unpredictable. It's a classic example of an unstoppable force versus an immovable object: an unbeaten Chiefs team hosting a winless Los Angeles squad desperate for answers. KC is among the favorites in the AFC to reach the Super Bowl in early projections. Patrick Mahomes is back to his MVP form after tearing his ACL against this same Chargers team a year ago, and the addition of running back Kenneth Walker has transformed the offense into a juggernaut. Can LA turn its campaign around and pull off an upset in Arrowhead Stadium this weekend? Let's take a look at what ESPN's Matchup Predictor says heading into kickoff. Chargers at Chiefs: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction Justin Herbert and Mahomes have had some great battles over the years, though this matchup comes under unusual circumstances. The Chargers haven't started a season 0-5 since the team was still based in San Diego more than 20 years ago. Dec 14, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) looks to pass against the Los Angeles Chargers during the second quarter at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 73.5%, Chargers 26.3%. Despite their dismal record, the Chargers still have a decent chance of coming out on top Sunday, according to the matchup predictor. For context, before the bye, the computer model only gave the Chiefs a 3.5% greater chance of beating an undefeated Raiders team on the road. Chiefs on SI's Take The Chargers are far out of the divisional race and likely out of playoff contention, but Jim Harbaugh's squad isn't as awful as its start suggests. It's hard to imagine a team of this caliber finishing with just four or five wins. LA suffered inexplicable defeats to the Raiders and Cardinals early in the season. Just when they appeared poised to finally get into the win column last week, the Chargers collapsed in the fourth quarter against fellow AFC West opponent, the Denver Broncos. Kansas City enters the game at 4-0 after winning its first four contests, while Los Angeles is searching for its first victory after opening the season 0-5. The Chargers will have a difficult challenge at Arrowhead Stadium as they try to turn their season around against one of the AFC's early standouts. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Patrick Mahomes Leads the Chiefs Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has helped Kansas City get off to an impressive start in 2026. Through four games, Mahomes has thrown for 1,037 yards and nine touchdowns with just two interceptions, giving the Chiefs a productive passing attack. Kansas City has also found success on the ground with running back Kenneth Walker III. Walker has rushed for 537 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 6.2 yards per carry. His ability to produce explosive runs has given opposing defenses another major concern beyond Mahomes. Head coach Andy Reid will look to keep that offensive balance going against a Chargers defense that has shown the ability to pressure quarterbacks. The Chiefs will also monitor wide receiver Rashee Rice, who missed practice Wednesday with a hamstring injury. Justin Herbert Faces a Difficult Challenge For Los Angeles, quarterback Justin Herbert needs to help an offense that has struggled to produce consistently. Herbert has thrown for 937 yards, five touchdowns and seven interceptions through five games. The Chargers have averaged only 16.8 points per game, making offensive improvement a major priority. Herbert has the arm talent to challenge Kansas City's secondary, but he will need better protection and consistent production from his receiving corps. Injuries have complicated that task, with several Los Angeles wide receivers and defensive starters appearing on the team's injury report this week. Head coach Jim Harbaugh must find a way to help his team limit mistakes and sustain drives. A stronger running game could ease the pressure on Herbert and help keep Mahomes off the field. Andy Reid vs. Jim Harbaugh The coaching matchup adds another layer to this divisional rivalry. Reid has Kansas City playing efficient football on both sides of the ball, while Harbaugh is trying to find answers after a difficult opening month. The Chargers swept the Chiefs in 2025, adding extra motivation for Kansas City to protect its home field and maintain control of the AFC West rivalry. A Critical AFC West Matchup Kansas City has an opportunity to improve to 5-0 and continue building momentum after its bye week. Los Angeles, meanwhile, needs a complete performance to avoid falling further behind in the division. Mahomes and Walker give the Chiefs multiple ways to attack, while Herbert will need to deliver a more consistent performance to help the Chargers compete. With the Chiefs chasing another strong start and the Chargers desperate to get their season moving, Sunday's matchup carries plenty of importance for both teams.

picks.blurb: NFL Week 6 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Another Packers-Cowboys clash, Raiders scare Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Broncos defeat Seahawks in OT Jordan Love | GettyImages | Illustration by Michael Castillo Cody Williams Tue, October 13, 2026 at 5:54 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The unbeatable Los Angeles Rams superteam is now 2-3 on the 2026 NFL season. The Houston Texans just got their first win. The Dallas Cowboys can't get out of their own way, and the Buffalo Bills are mauling everyone in their way. It's been a wacky start to the season, which has made our NFL picks and predictions for every game each week a bit more difficult than I expected. We're having to adjust our perceptions and expectations on the fly, and we're still in the mix as we head into what should be a fascinating Week 6. Zach Rotman came out of the bullpen for me last week and came through with a solid week. Many, many thanks to him for helping the cause, but I'm back in the saddle now. Let's hope I don't make this thing go any further off the rails, but let's dive right into this fun slate with our NFL picks for Week 6 as we make predictions both straight-up and against the spread for all 14 games on the slate this week. NFL Week 6 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game NFL Week 6 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Seahawks vs. Broncos (TNF) Seahawks -2.5 Texans vs. Jaguars (London) Bears vs. Falcons Ravens vs. Browns Jets vs. Patriots Patriots -7.5 Saints vs. Giants Titans vs. Colts Panthers vs. Eagles Panthers +1.5 Steelers vs. Buccaneers Steelers -2.5 Cardinals vs. Rams Bills vs. Raiders Chargers vs. Chiefs Cowboys vs. Packers Commanders vs. 49ers 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 51-28 (Last week 9-6) | ATS Record: 37-40-2 (Last week 8-7) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 6 prediction to make Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders (+5.5) The Buffalo Bills have been rolling, including toppling the Rams in overtime in Los Angeles on Monday night. Stop me if you've heard this one before, but Buffalo has one of the NFL's best offenses behind Josh Allen and it doesn't seem like there's a defense in the league that's going to be able to stop this team from scoring 30 points - they're quite literally averaging 32.7 points per game after the first five games of the year. Meanwhile, the Raiders have certainly fallen back to earth a bit, losing two straight after their 3-0 start to the season. At the same time, the Bills defense is the same problem it's been for the past few years. It seems like Buffalo has to produce at this level offensively to win games because the defense is going to give it up. While the Raiders might not be a surprise contender, they still look like a quite competent football team behind Kirk Cousins and, while Buffalo will be able to score on their defense, they're still averaging 26.4 points per game on the year. I think Buffalo still has the offensive firepower against a middling defense to get the win in this game. But with it being in Vegas against a team that has a legitimate pulse, it's going to be another shootout and one that could likely be decided by a field goal once again. 5.5 points is a bit too many, so we'll take the Raiders against the spread and pray. Easiest NFL Week 6 pick on the board Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) This line could've been two touchdowns and I'm still taking the Kansas City Chiefs over the division rival Chargers. For starters, what has LA shown this season to make you believe they have a chance in Arrowhead in Week 6? No, seriously. There's been little evidence to think that this game will be close as the Chiefs have been absolutely rolling on both sides of the ball while Justin Herbert delivers the worst season of his career, the Chargers defense is middling at its best and the self-inflicted wounds in each game from LA multiply likes the heads of a hydra. If that weren't enough, Andy Reid is famously one of the most lethal head coaches when his team is coming off of the bye week. This isn't to say that the Chiefs are a perfect team as I maintain that they still need to find some more upgrades at wide receiver, especially after the gnarly Tyquan Thornton injury. While that may be true, though, they are a far better coached and more talented team than the winless Chargers and I wouldn't be surprised if this game was lopsided and out of hand early in favor of the home side. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Coming off of a home loss to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and the previously winless Buccaneers, naturally I'm taking the Dallas Cowboys to go on the road to Lambeau and beat the Packers as underdogs. What about this doesn't make sense to you? Yes, the optics look strange. However, this isn't about expecting the Cowboys hiring Mike Pettine to essentially help out new defensive coordinator Christian Parker drastically improving the defense, though it can't hurt. It's more about this being a likely shootout between these two teams because, despite what happened to Tyson Bagent and the Bears, I still don't trust Green Bay on that side of the ball. Furthermore, I also still don't trust the Packers run game, even against Dallas. Expect this game to go back and forth throughout the action, but I believe the Cowboys are going to have more offensive firepower and some adjustments on the side of the ball you can actually trust Dallas on to attack Green Bay throughout. They might not come up with many stops of their own, but they'll have enough to pull out the win. Plus, just from a narrative perspective, if ever there was a time for the Cowboys to keep their fans from abandoning ship, it's a game like this, and this franchise has been masterful at doing exactly that over the years.
